note: How long one application at the label rate keeps protecting a crop in hot, wet, sunny Philippine fields. Herbicide days are how long the treated ground stays weed controlled.

Chlorpyrifos.note: Contact and vapor action; a leaf spray fades within a week in hot weather.

Chlorpyrifos methyl.note: Short lived in the field; on stored grain it guards for months.

Profenofos.note: Strong contact kill on caterpillars and mites, but little lasting cover.

Diazinon.note: A spray lasts several days; granules in paddy water hold a week or two.

Quinalphos.note: Contact organophosphate; heat, sun and rain wear it off within about a week.

Triazophos.note: Contact with some depth into the leaf; about a week of cover.

Azamethiphos.note: Fly bait and spray for sheds; works while the deposit stays dry.

Cadusafos.note: Soil nematicide; guards roots for about six weeks after placement.

Fosthiazate.note: Soil applied; moves into roots and holds nematodes back for about six weeks.

Terbufos.note: Soil granule that guards roots and seedlings for about a month or more.

Fenamiphos.note: Soil nematicide; about six weeks of root protection in moist soil.

Monocrotophos.note: Highly toxic systemic; about a week of cover on sucking pests.

Methamidophos.note: Highly toxic systemic; about a week of cover.

Ethoprophos.note: Soil nematicide and insecticide; about six weeks of cover around roots.

Dichlorvos.note: Acts as a vapor and is gone within a day or two.

Trichlorfon.note: Breaks down quickly, mostly in alkaline water; only a few days of cover.

Methidathion.note: Contact organophosphate; heat, sun and rain wear it off within about a week.

Phosalone.note: Longer lasting than most of its group; about ten days of cover.

Prothiofos.note: Contact organophosphate; heat, sun and rain wear it off within about a week.

Temephos.note: Larvicide for standing water; keeps mosquito larvae down for weeks.

Isazofos.note: Soil applied; guards roots for about a month.

Carbaryl.note: Quick contact kill that breaks down within days in the field.

Methomyl.note: Fast contact and stomach kill with only a few days of cover.

Carbofuran.note: Granules in soil or paddy water move into the plant and protect for weeks.

Carbosulfan.note: A spray lasts about a week; as a seed treatment it guards seedlings longer.

Thiodicarb.note: Larvae must eat it; about a week of cover, longer as a seed treatment.

Isoprocarb (MIPC).note: Quick hopper knockdown with very short cover.

Oxamyl.note: Moves up and down the plant; about ten days on pests and nematodes.

Propoxur.note: Quick contact kill that breaks down within days in the field.

Metolcarb.note: Quick contact kill that breaks down within days in the field.

Benfuracarb.note: Soil or seed applied; guards seedlings for a couple of weeks.

Furathiocarb.note: Seed treatment that guards young plants for their first weeks.

Formetanate.note: Quick contact kill that breaks down within days in the field.

Aldicarb.note: Soil granule taken up by roots; protects for about six weeks.

Bendiocarb.note: Mainly for buildings and stores, where surface deposits last longer.

Gamma cyhalothrin.note: Fast knockdown on contact; strong sun breaks it down within a week.

Zeta cypermethrin.note: Fast knockdown on contact; strong sun breaks it down within a week.

Cypermethrin.note: Fast knockdown on contact; sun and heat break it down within a week.

Deltamethrin.note: Potent contact kill; sun and rain leave about five days of cover.

Bifenthrin.note: One of the longest lasting pyrethroids on leaves and in soil.

Etofenprox.note: Contact kill with low fish risk, used on rice hoppers; about five days of cover.

Permethrin.note: Fast knockdown on contact; strong sun breaks it down within a week.

Fenpropathrin.note: Contact kill on insects and mites; about a week of cover.

Cyhalothrin.note: Fast knockdown on contact; strong sun breaks it down within a week.

Transfluthrin.note: Vapor action in coils and indoor emitters; no field cover.

Silafluofen.note: Contact kill with somewhat longer life than most of its kind.

Chlorfenapyr.note: Acts over a day or two; about a week of cover on caterpillars and mites.

Indoxacarb.note: Larvae stop feeding within hours after eating it; about a week of cover.

Metaflumizone.note: Larvae must eat it; about ten days of cover.

Chlorfluazuron.note: Stops young larvae molting, so kill is slow but cover lasts about two weeks.

Teflubenzuron.note: Stops young larvae molting, so kill is slow but cover lasts about two weeks.

Flufenoxuron.note: Stops young larvae molting, so kill is slow but cover lasts about two weeks.

Triflumuron.note: Stops young larvae molting, so kill is slow but cover lasts about two weeks.

Pyridalyl.note: Contact and stomach action on caterpillars and thrips; about a week of cover.

Hexythiazox.note: Kills mite eggs and young, not adults; slow start but long cover.

Fenpyroximate.note: Fast mite kill on contact with about two weeks of cover.

Tolfenpyrad.note: Contact kill on thrips, caterpillars and mites; about a week of cover.

Fenazaquin.note: Fast mite kill on contact with about two weeks of cover.

Pyridaben.note: Contact mite and whitefly kill with about two weeks of cover.

Afidopyropen.note: Aphids and whiteflies stop feeding fast; about ten days of cover.

Flometoquin.note: Fast thrips kill on contact; about a week of cover.

Etoxazole.note: Stops mite eggs and young developing; slow start but long cover.

Rotenone.note: Botanical that light breaks down within a few days.

Bromadiolone.note: One feed can kill, but rats die after four to seven days; keep bait stations stocked.
